solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stupor by battle site after soldiers protest

indicators.note: the battle site is placed after the soldiers in the build
the stupor sits beside, that is next to, the battle site

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the army's sappers
Mons in Belgium was the scene of a famous 1914 battle
a trance is a dazed, stupefied state

explanation.surface: A soldier dazed after fighting at a battlefield makes a formal complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Mons, in Belgium, was the first big British battle of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A remonstrance is a forceful formal complaint, a synonym of the noun protest.

clue.text: Shape of abandoned ship reportedly on seaweed

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
signals that the word for the ship is taken by how it is said, not how it is spelt

parts.note: a ship left as a ruin is a wreck
tangle is a name for kelp-type seaweed

explanation.surface: A sunken hulk lying on a bed of weed has an outline worth describing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes WRECK sound as REC; tangle is a little-known name for a kind of large seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectangle is an example of a geometric figure, a four-sided one with right angles.

clue.text: Insects would get this holy man outside South American capital

indicators.note: the holy man's name is the part lying outside the capital within the insects, so the capital is taken away

parts.note: mosquitoes are biting insects
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A riddle about what bugs would make of a prophet wrapped round a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it backwards: put the holy man outside QUITO and you get the insects; so the insects minus the capital leave him. 'would get this' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Moses is the Old Testament prophet and lawgiver, a classic example of a holy man.

clue.text: Food in tin served up, spicy but lacking first hint of taste

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for the tin is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: tells us the spicy word loses a letter

parts.note: spicy food is hot

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word taste is what goes missing

explanation.surface: A tinned snack is dished up, hot but somehow without flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses CAN to NAC; 'lacking first hint of taste' drops T from HOT, leaving HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla-chip snack, an example of Mexican-style food.

clue.text: Historian has time to celebrate American getting rid of king

parts.note: to revel is to make merry

indicators.note: the American word sheds one letter

parts.note: a Yank is an informal word for an American
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A scholar takes time off to party with an American who has dethroned a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: G. M. Trevelyan was a celebrated English historian of the twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: George Macaulay Trevelyan wrote famous histories of England, so he is an example of a historian.

clue.text: Plant, say, found on island? Eagle circles round it

indicators.note: the eagle's word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: aquila is Latin for eagle, also the name of a constellation
EG, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: An island plant is spotted while an eagle wheels over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the EG plus I that the eagle encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquilegia is the columbine, a garden flower and so an example of a plant.

clue.text: A gypsy man that's caught on the rebound

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is placed on top of what follows

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a Rom is a Romany man

explanation.surface: A traveller is caught out after bouncing back from heartbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rebound' suggests romance, but the rebound is a ball bouncing off.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a carom is a shot where the ball bounces off another, hence a rebound.

clue.text: Skilled speakers that may give heroic rants, I fancy

indicators.note: used as an adjective, fancy means elaborate or rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Orators are the sort who might deliver grand, heroic tirades.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoricians are experts in persuasive oratory, people practised at public speaking.

clue.text: Journalists in shed, first to last

indicators.note: the shed word's opening letter is taken to its end

parts.note: a shack is a rough shed

explanation.surface: Reporters are working out of a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving S from the front of SHACK to the back gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks is a mildly scornful slang word for newspaper writers.

clue.text: Bank document with particular colour and with particular design

parts.note: a cheque is a written order to a bank to pay
red is one specific colour

explanation.surface: A banker describes a cheque printed in a certain shade and pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Chequered means patterned with squares, a specific kind of design.

clue.text: Good tendrils could excite this type of plant expert

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Fine climbing shoots might thrill a botanist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dendrologist studies trees, a specialist branch of botany.

clue.text: Swap parts one's wrongly positioned

indicators.note: letters placed in the wrong spots need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone tells a mechanic to exchange components fitted in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: To transpose is to make two things change places, the same as a verb meaning exchange.

clue.text: Maiden squeezed by thin old lover

indicators.note: the maiden letter is held tightly within the thin word

parts.note: lean means thin
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A young woman is hugged by her skinny former boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden in cricket is an over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Leman is an archaic word for a sweetheart or paramour.

clue.text: Conservative perhaps wanting a strategy immediately

parts.note: a Conservative belongs to the political right
a way is a method or plan

explanation.surface: A Tory politician demands a plan without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at once, without any delay, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: How to start preparing soup? Assess the situation

definitions.meaning: soup begins with taking some broth base, read literally
to review where things stand before acting

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to review circumstances, while literally you take broth base to begin a soup.

clue.text: Shabby message from a happy early bird?

definitions.text: message from a happy early bird?
definitions.meaning: the early bird catches its prey and gleefully reports its meal consumed

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says the early bird catches the worm; a satisfied bird might announce exactly what it has done.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood riddled by grubs looks decrepit, so the adjective figuratively means old and tatty.

clue.text: Animal with gross exterior gets one staring

indicators.note: the gross letters form the outside, around the animal

parts.note: GR is an abbreviation for gross, as in weight
an ape is an animal

explanation.surface: A beast with a revolting outside draws an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaper is someone who gawps open-mouthed, an onlooker.

clue.text: Following summary, see without a doubt

indicators.note: the see comes after the summary

parts.note: a précis is a short summary
Ely is a cathedral city and diocese, and a see is a bishop's diocese

explanation.surface: After reading the synopsis, you will see it is certainly true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like a verb but is the bishop's seat, here the diocese of Ely in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Precisely is used as an emphatic reply meaning exactly so, quite certain.

clue.text: Hear a sound sound

indicators.note: tells us the inlet word is taken as spoken, then respelt

parts.note: a sound is an inlet of sea, as is a creek

explanation.surface: An instruction to listen, with a word stammered twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'sound' is a narrow sea channel; the second is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A creak is a squeaky grating noise, an example of a sound.

clue.text: Phone everyone, be involved to stir a distant memory?

parts.note: to ring is to phone

indicators.note: be is wrapped up within the everyone word

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Calling all your friends to get them on board might jog a recollection.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something that seems vaguely familiar, prompting recall.

clue.text: Girls heading off, not the most sensible types

indicators.note: the girls word loses its first letter

parts.note: lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Young women set off, though they are hardly the wisest.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are foolish people, those short on good sense.

clue.text: Brown water in which Greek character is immersed

indicators.note: the Greek letter is plunged into the water word

parts.note: the sea is water
pi is a Greek letter

explanation.surface: A Greek is swimming in muddy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown tint, as in old photographs.

clue.text: This writer's suffering setback, crazy and getting on

indicators.note: a setback turns the setter's word backwards

parts.note: this writer is the setter, me; the 's means is, linking to the setback
barking is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: The setter, having a reverse, is going mad and boarding.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking, short for barking mad, is British slang for insane.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarking means boarding a ship or plane, that is getting on.

clue.text: Hospital food served up in Scottish town once

indicators.note: in a down clue the hospital and food letters are written upwards

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Hospital meals are dished out in an old Scottish settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgh was a Scottish chartered borough, an administrative status now abolished.

clue.text: Express identity with introductory chat

indicators.note: the chat word comes first, introducing the identity letters

parts.note: rap is slang for talk or chat
ID is short for identity

explanation.surface: A personal statement gets a short preface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like a verb but is the adjective, as in an express train.
explanation.definitionFit: An express service is fast, so the adjective means quick.

clue.text: One helping senior copper outside Dover?

indicators.note: the police officer goes around the harbour word

parts.note: a super, short for superintendent, is a senior police officer
Dover is a Channel port, an example signalled by the question mark

explanation.surface: A police chief lends a hand on the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Dover is a major English port on the Channel coast in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter is a backer, someone who assists.

clue.text: Iron Lady exuding energy repeatedly

indicators.note: to exude is to give off, so letters leave the lady

parts.note: a peeress is a titled lady

indicators.note: the energy letter is taken twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher, the Iron Lady, keeps pouring out energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron Lady' reads as Thatcher's nickname, but Iron is the verb and Lady is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to iron them, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Like worker returning home from night shift years ago?

definitions.text: Like worker returning home from night shift
definitions.meaning: after a night shift the worker comes home again during daylight

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in the old days, while literally it is home again in daylight hours.
